About Us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the Employer
We are supporting a care services provider based in Darwin and surrounding areas, operating in the aged care, disability support, and community services sector. The business is known for its commitment to compassionate, respectful, and person-centred care, supporting clients to maintain their dignity, independence, wellbeing, and quality of life. With a growing team and services delivered across multiple client locations, they are seeking to fill the role of Aged or Disabled Carer. This opportunity offers stable employment, meaningful hands-on care work, and the chance to be part of a supportive and inclusive work environment focused on making a positive difference in people’s lives.

About the Role
As an Aged or Disabled Carer, you will provide practical and emotional support to clients who are aged, living with disability, or require assistance with daily activities. The role requires patience, respect, strong communication skills, and a genuine commitment to improving the quality of life of vulnerable clients.

Key Responsibilities
The successful applicant will be responsible for:
- Providing personal care support, including hygiene, grooming, dressing, toileting, and mobility assistance
- Supporting clients with daily living activities in their home and community
- Assisting with meal preparation, feeding support, and basic household tasks
- Supporting clients to attend appointments, social activities, and community participation
- Monitoring client wellbeing and reporting any changes, concerns, incidents, or risks to the supervisor
- Providing companionship and emotional support in a respectful and professional manner
- Following individual care plans, workplace policies, and NDIS-related requirements
- Maintaining accurate records, progress notes, and communication with relevant team members
- Assisting with safe manual handling and mobility support, where required
- Promoting client independence, dignity, choice, and privacy at all times

Selection Criteria
Applicants should be able to demonstrate:
1. Experience providing care or support to aged persons, people with disability, or vulnerable clients
2. A caring, patient, respectful, and reliable approach to client support
3. Good communication skills and ability to follow care instructions
4. Ability to assist with personal care and daily living tasks
5. Understanding of confidentiality, duty of care, and client dignity
6. Ability to work independently and as part of a small care team
7. Flexibility to work across different shifts, including weekends where required
8. Commitment to safe work practices, infection control, and client wellbeing

Required Experience and Qualifications
- Minimum 1–2 years of relevant care/support experience preferred
- Relevant qualification in aged care, disability support, individual support, community services, or similar field is preferred but not mandatory
- Current First Aid and CPR certificate, or willingness to obtain
- NDIS Worker Screening Check, or willingness to obtain
- National Police Check, or willingness to obtain
- Driver licence and access to reliable transport is preferred
- Full working rights in Australia

How to Apply
We are looking for a compassionate, reliable, and safety-minded Aged or Disabled Carer to support clients with daily living activities and help promote their independence, dignity, wellbeing, and quality of life.

To apply, please submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter of no more than 300 words explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork. Please use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action,
Result.
- A written response of no more than 600 words describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role. Please structure your example or examples using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a caring and supportive community services business that values compassion, respect, safety, dignity, and person-centred care, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Phone calls and walk-in applications will not be accepted.

Applications close: 04 August 2026

Just Better Care Eastern Suburbs 

Full-Time Disabilities Services Officer (Multiple positions) 

About us:
Just Better Care provides in-home disability and aged care services, supporting people to live independently. We believe people of all ages & all abilities deserve access to the support and resources they need in order to live where they want and how they want. At Just Better Care, we CARE about our customers and our team. Our office covers four territories in the Sydney Metro area; Eastern Suburbs, Inner West, Sutherland and St George.
Just Better Care Eastern Suburb is looking for Disabilities Services Officer to join our caring and dynamic team. This role involves working with customers to support them in many different aspects of their day-to-day life. The role involves supporting customers with mental, physical, social and emotional disabilities. Support is provided in a manner that maintains the customer’s independence, is respectful and safe.

Main responsibility
•	Demonstrate a commitment to best practice, ensuring that all services are provided in a caring and respectful way in accordance with Just Better Care’s policy and procedures.
•	Assisting clients in showering, dressing, grooming, manual transfers and hoist assisted.
•	Social support/transportation: social activities, shopping/groceries, travelling to medical appointments
•	Clinical support: medication assistance, catheter, bowel care, enteral feeding,
•	Supporting customers in the use of aids and personal equipment including: standing or walking frames, wheelchairs, manual or electric hoists, sliding sheets or moving boards, hearing aids and other physical aids
•	Supporting customers with complex and/or challenging behaviours
•	Monitoring the well-being of customers and reporting on their progress
•	Providing a safe environment for the client by monitoring their surroundings for potential dangers such as fire hazards and tripping hazards.
•	Supporting clients socially and arranging visits or outings in the community.
•	Ensuring that all documentation is completed in a timely and accurate manner. Where offices are using Mobility Options, community support workers are required to use the application for all schedule visits as per their training.
•	Attending and participating in staff meetings and training sessions as directed by the Coordinator.
•	Ensuring that all responsible steps are taken to protect personal safety at work and avoid adversely affecting the health or safety of any other person at the workplace in accordance with requirements under the Work Health and Safety legalisation.
•	Participating in activities aimed at the continuous improvement of services.
•	Complying with Just Better Care’s Vision, Values, and Purpose

What you will need:
•	Qualification in the relevant field.
•	At least 2 years’ relevant work experience.
•	NDIS Workers Check or Police Clearance
•	Current Australian Drivers Licence
•	Current First Aid and CPR certificates
•	Ability to be contacted by either telephone or email
•	Ability or willingness to assist or work with customer in daily living and personal care skills
•	Be reliable & productive
•	Valuing attitudes towards customers
•	Ability to work as part of a Team and maintain good working relationships
•	Commitment to self-improvement
•	Good written and verbal skills in English

Salary Range: $80,000 to 90,000 per annum excluding superannuation.
Why Join Us: 
•	Close-knit team of friendly, helpful and supportive people.
•	Career development and training opportunities are very high on our priority list.
•	We have a vested interest in you, hence you will be well supported.
•	A competitive salary is on offer for the right candidate.
•	Employee Assistance Programme.
If you have any questions or would like to know more about the role, send an e-mail to hr.es@justbettercare.com

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Your role at St John of God Accord

We are looking for a dedicated Positive Behaviour Support Practitioner (Grade 1 or 2) to join our community disability team on an up to permanent, full-time basis, part-time considered with a minimum of 0.6 FTE.

St John of God Accord (Accord) is a values-focused disability service provider in Victoria. We partner with people with disabilities to empower them to live a great life, with a full range of tailored services. We welcome people of all diverse identities, religious and cultural backgrounds.

We provide a wide range of NDIS services to over 1,000 people with disabilities for:

Specialist allied health services such as Positive Behaviour Support, Psychology Occupational Therapy, Speech Pathology, and Music Therapy

Long term homes and short-term respite, for supported independent living and respite (STA)

Skill-building through support coordination, group programs and individualised support in the community

This role presents an exceptional opportunity to deliver high-quality, person-centred care within a value's focused, family-friendly, not-for-profit organisation with offices in Greensborough and Scoresby, and access to any Waterman Office Suite across Victoria.

The Position

Delivering direct, evidence-based occupational therapy services to individuals or groups, primarily in community settings for NDIS participants.

Conducting thorough assessments such as the Functional Behaviour Assessment and World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule

Developing and implementing comprehensive behaviour support plans, ensuring appropriate progression towards people's goals.

Coordinating the provision of specialised supports and other care team members to improve people's quality of life and address behaviours of concern.

Providing consultation and support as part of a multidisciplinary allied health team.

Ensuring all practice adheres to the relevant legislation, Code of Ethics and St John of God Health Care policies and guidelines.

We are seeking a qualified and motivated Positive Behaviour Support practitioner who has a tertiary qualification in: Psychology, Social Work, Occupational Therapy, Speech Pathology, Applied Behaviour Analysis-Behavioural Science, Disability, Mental Health or Education and-or a relevant qualification in Positive Behaviour Support (associated specialty registrations such as AHPRA-eligibility for registration with AASW will be required).

You will be suitability to be registered by the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission as a Behaviour Support Practitioner (Core level minimum) and Demonstrate understanding of the principles of Positive Behaviour Support (PBS) and person-centred practice. The ideal candidate will have over 2 years' experience and tertiary level qualifications

Strong verbal and written communication abilities are essential, along with the capacity to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a dynamic team, will be essential to this role.

Successful applicants must hold a NDIS Screening Number, Victoria Drivers License and current First Aid certificate.

Above all, person-centred care will be at the core of everything you do committing to and supporting our Mission and Values.

We can offer you

Salary packaging up to $18,550 on a range of benefits such as mortgage, rent, meal entertainment, holiday accommodation or other everyday living expenses as well as options to salary package benefits above the FBT cap on items such as:

Novated leasing 

work related expenses

self-education and

additional superannuation

•	Full-Time Bricklayer (Blocklayer)
•	Salary Range: $75,000 - $95,000 per annum plus superannuation
•	Exciting opportunity to work in a professional setting.

About Us
Monolith Civil Australia is a premier civil construction and infrastructure contractor. We deliver large-scale commercial, industrial, and public infrastructure projects across Australia. We are committed to safety, structural integrity, and operational excellence. Our teams work on complex civil engineering projects requiring high-quality masonry, blockwork, and structural bricklaying.

About the role
The Bricklayer (Blocklayer) is responsible for constructing, repairing, and maintaining brick, block, and stone structures across various civil construction sites. This role requires precision in laying materials for retaining walls, structural foundations, and infrastructure components. The successful candidate will interpret architectural plans, calculate material requirements, and execute masonry work to strict Australian Standards and project specifications.

Duties and Responsibilities

•	Study blueprints, civil engineering drawings, and specifications to determine material requirements, dimensions, and installation procedures.
•	Seal foundations with damp-resistant materials to prevent moisture ingress.
•	Prepare mortar mixtures to correct consistencies and spread mortar accurately for structural integrity.
•	Lay bricks, stone, structural tiles, and heavy concrete building blocks in specified rows, designs, and shapes.
•	Check the vertical and horizontal alignment of structures continuously using plumb bobs, spirit levels, and laser levels.
•	Cut, shape, and polish stones, bricks, and blocks using specialized masonry saws and hand tools to fit custom spaces.
•	Build retaining walls, structural pillars, manholes, and other masonry components required for civil infrastructure projects.
•	Repair and maintain existing brick, cement block, and related masonry structures on site.
•	Comply with all Monolith Civil Australia Work Health and Safety (WHS) policies and procedures.
•	Erect and dismantle scaffolding safely to facilitate masonry work at heights.
•	Identify and report site hazards, near misses, and incidents to the Site Supervisor immediately.
•	Ensure all masonry work complies with the Building Code of Australia (BCA) and relevant structural engineering standards.

Essential Skills

•	Advanced ability to read and interpret complex civil construction plans and structural diagrams.
•	Strong spatial awareness and ability to calculate material quantities accurately.
•	High level of physical fitness and stamina to perform manual labour, lift heavy materials, and work in various weather conditions.
•	Exceptional precision in alignment, leveling, and finishing of masonry structures.

Qualifications needed:

•	Minimum Trade qualification certificate or equivalent relevant work experience
•	Minimum one year of work experience on relevant position
•	White card
•	Driver’s License

What We Offer

•	Competitive salary based on experience
•	Opportunities for professional growth and training
•	A supportive and dynamic work environment
•	Work on exciting projects with cutting-edge technology

Salary:  The role offers a remuneration package ranging from $75,000-$95,000 plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

result.description:
Location: 		Kenmore, QLD, 4069
Full-Time: 		Immediate start
Reports to:		Facility Manager
Job Title: 		Community Worker - Disability
Salary range: 		$79,500 - $85,000 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date:	30 days

About the Role
On behalf of our client, a registered NDIS provider dedicated to empowering individuals to “live well,” we are seeking a dedicated Community Worker – Disability. Our client specialises in Supported Independent Living (SIL), Short Term Accommodation, Community Access, Allied Health/Therapeutic Support, and Behaviour Support for children and adults with disabilities or developmental delays. Their focus is on building daily living skills, fostering community participation, and providing a “home away from home.” We are looking for a worker who will assist clients to solve social, emotional, and practical problems while promoting genuine independence.

Key Duties (paraphrased & detailed)
Assessment & Program Development
• Assess clients’ needs, abilities, and personal goals, then plan, develop, and implement individualized educational, training, and support programs (e.g., daily living skills, community access, therapeutic activities).
• Interview clients and their families to determine the nature and extent of social, emotional, financial, or behavioural difficulties, using this information to tailor NDIS-funded supports.

Monitoring & Referral
• Monitor and report regularly on clients’ progress toward their SIL or community participation goals, adjusting support strategies as needed.
• Refer clients to additional agencies or allied health professionals (e.g., behavior support practitioners, community nurses) when specialized help is required.

Community & Resource Liaison
• Assess community needs and available resources for health, welfare, housing, employment, training, and other disability-specific facilities, then connect clients accordingly.
• Liaise with community groups, government bodies, private businesses, and other welfare agencies to promote awareness of disability resources and advocate for client inclusion.

Direct Support & Family Assistance
• Support families and provide education, personal care, and social engagement for disabled persons in adult service units, group housing, or short-term accommodation settings.
• Assist young people and adults to solve social, emotional, and financial problems, including budgeting, accessing transport, or managing challenging behaviours using tailored behaviour support plans.

Administration & Funding
• Prepare clear, timely submissions for funding and resources, including reports to government bodies (e.g., NDIA) and other agencies, ensuring compliance with NDIS Practice Standards.

Skills & Experience Required
• Minimum 1 year full-time relevant experience (disability support, community services, or allied health assistance).
• Relevant qualification (e.g., Certificate IV/Diploma in Community Services, Disability, or Mental Health).
• Current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance (preferable), satisfactory police check, valid driver’s license, and own transport.
• Up-to-date flu vaccination and COVID-19 immunization (as required).

Why Join?
Rewarding work that empowers clients to live well, ongoing training, supportive team culture, and modern community-based facilities.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.
